newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Peace force in Central African Republic clash.
newsitem.headline: Peace force in Central African Republic clash.

text.p: Units of an African peacekeeping force in the Central African Republic capital Bangui clashed with unreconciled army mutineers on Friday and pushed them back to one of their strongholds, witnesses said.

The reason for the clash was not immediately clear. It was the first such incident since a failed attempt to reintegrate mutineers from the paramilitary gendarmerie into their units under a January 25 peace plan to end the country's third army mutiny in under a year.
Officials say talks have begun to find ways of reintegrating the gendarmes in their units as has been the case with other members of the armed forces.
A standoff between members of President Ange-Felix Patasse's presidential guard and gendarmes who joined the mutiny prevented an earlier attempt to reintegrate the gendarmes into the unit on June 13.

An African force, which includes soldiers from Burkina Faso, Chad, Gabon, Mali, Senegal and Togo, deployed in Bangui under a peace accord brokered by Mali's widely respected former military leader Amadou Toumani Toure in January.
It is a likely model for efforts to broker peace in Brazzaville, capital of the neighbouring Congo Republic where similar political and ethnic clashes broke out on June 5.
The first mutinies, in April and May 1996, began as protests over pay but became a movement to topple Patasse, a northern civilian elected in 1993.
The third mutiny began in November and degenerated into ethnic bloodshed. French troops, in the country under a defence pact, restored order and handed over to the African force.
The mutineers are principally from the southern Yakoma tribe of former military leader Andre Kolongba.
